newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia state forestry firms '97 profit seen down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia state forestry firms '97 profit seen down.

text.p: Indonesia said on Wednesday pre-tax profit of its six state-owned forestry firms was seen falling to 227.32 billion rupiah in 1997 from an expected 275.06 billion rupiah in 1996.

Forestry Minister Djamaluddin Soeryohadikusumo said in a statement to a parliamentary committee hearing that the firms were expected to book total sales of 1.61 trillion rupiah in 1997 against an expected 1.20 trillion rupiah in 1996.
Djamaluddin said the six firms posted pre-tax profit of 262.92 billion rupiah in 1995 on total sales of 933.5 billion rupiah.
The six firms are Perum Perhutani and PT Inhutani I to V, he said.
Djamaluddin said the government was considering setting up a new forestry firm to be called PT Inhutani VI which could take place in 1998 at the latest.
Inhutani VI's core business would be planting, processing and selling forestry products like the other Inhutani companies, he said. Its forest area would be in eastern Indonesia, he added.
Djamaluddin did not give further details.
